prompt:
I need the front end for Slotdesk. The in-house production system a large metropolitan newspaper's copy desk uses to move between print editions, sections, page layouts and their corresponding web stories during nightly production.

Who's using it: Marguerite Fontaine, 52, the night slot editor at a major metro daily. She has run the copy desk for nine years and oversees 6 copy editors and 2 page designers each night across three regional print zones. She knows the paper's structure cold but works under severe time pressure.

What they're doing right now: It's 10:40 pm, 25 minutes before the first-edition deadline. The city council just voted 7–6 to approve the transit levy, so the A1 lead story in the Metro zone must be rewritten and its jump page changed. She needs to get from the Metro A1 to the story's slot on the budget, then to the jump on B4, then to the North and South zone versions, which carry a different second-day reference. After that she checks the live web version of the story, and gets back to where she was to sign off the remaining sports pages. She can't afford to lose her place.

What's in the system at this point: Tonight's paper: Monday 23 Nov 2026, 3 zones (Metro, North, South), each with sections A (News, 14 pages), B (Local, 10), C (Sports, 12) and D (Life, 8). There are 2 editions, first (deadline 11:05 pm) and final (12:40 am). There are 87 stories on tonight's budget, each with a slug (for example 'COUNCIL-LEVY'), desk, reporter, assigned copy editor, length in inches, status (reporting, editing, slotted, proofed, sent), and the pages it appears on per zone and edition. COUNCIL-LEVY runs 28 inches, starting on A1 and jumping to B4 in Metro and to A6 in North and South. Its web counterpart was published at 10:31 pm with 3 updates. Pages signed off so far: 31 of 44 for Metro first edition. Sports still has 5 pages open, awaiting a West Coast game score.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
